To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thermal water disposal in arable land causes soil salinization/sodicity, soil degradation, salt accumulation in groundwater, and soil type change.

the investigated Chernozem, Phaeeozem and Arenosols were negatively affected by the thermal water seep, and the most vulnerable soils were Chernozem and Phaeeozem, while in Arenosol the thermal water did not reach the soil surface.

the investigated soil profiles are affected by thermal water seepages, and the most affected soils are Chernozem, and Phaeozem, where thermal water seeped into the soil and reached groundwater, which caused salinization and Na+ mobilization, respectively.

the long-term effects of thermal water disposal on the soil and groundwater quality of arable land.

the disposal of thermal water in an uncontrolled manner into a recipient surrounded by arable soil represents a serious risk to the environment.
thermal water seepages have a significant impact on the investigated soil types, and this impact can be detected even in the case of the most resistant soil type.
the disposal of thermal water into a surface channel is a potential environmental risk.

the disposal of waste thermal water can lead to soil degradation and groundwater contamination, especially in Chernozem and Phaeezem soils.
